statement: At 12:00 noon, Anne, Beth, and Carmen begin running laps around a circular track of length $300$ metres, all starting from the same point. Each jogger maintains a constant speed in one of the two possible directions indefinitely. Show that if Anne's speed is different from the other two speeds, then at some later time Anne will be at least $100$ metres from each of the other runners. (Distance is measured along the shorter of the two arcs separating two runners.)

A permutation of the integers $1901, 1902, \ldots, 2000$ is a sequence $a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_{100}$ in which each of those integers appears exactly once. Given such a permutation, form the sequence of partial sums
$$s_1 = a_1,\ s_2 = a_1 + a_2,\ \ldots,\ s_{100} = a_1 + a_2 + \cdots + a_{100}.$$
How many of these permutations have no term of the sequence $s_1, \ldots, s_{100}$ divisible by three?

Let $A = (a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_{2000})$ be a sequence of integers each lying in the interval $[-1000, 1000]$. Suppose the entries of $A$ sum to $1$. Show that some nonempty subsequence of $A$ sums to zero.
Let $ABCD$ be a convex quadrilateral with $\angle CBD = 2\angle ADB$, $\angle ABD = 2\angle CDB$, and $AB = CB$. Prove that $AD = CD$.

Suppose that the real numbers $a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_{100}$ satisfy
$$0 \leq a_{100} \leq a_{99} \leq \cdots \leq a_2 \leq a_1, \quad a_1 + a_2 \leq 100, \quad a_3 + a_4 + \cdots + a_{100} \leq 100.$$
Determine the maximum possible value of $a_1^2 + a_2^2 + \cdots + a_{100}^2$, and find all sequences which achieve this maximum.
